newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes stilled by NYMEX rally, sours bearish.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes stilled by NYMEX rally, sours bearish.

text.p: U.S. domestic crudes turned quiet thinned by the surprising rally in NYMEX crude futures with sours defensive on ample supplies, traders said.
Industry functions in Houston also stole participation in wet markets, causing most grades to stay ranged-bound.

November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $24.75-85 a barrel, 75 cents above Wednesday. The Nov/Dec WTI spread widened out to 60 cents from the low 50 cents, encouraged by a spurt in heating oil on colder weather in the U.S. northeast.
"We made up for three days going down 55 cents, taken that back and added to it," a Texas trader said.
Heavy, sour crudes moderated around the previous day's low levels, but bounced off intraday lows.
West Texas Sour/Midland, was reportedly traded at WTI minus $1.37 a barrel, and then at minus $1.35, some seven to eight cents lower than Wednesday.
The market for heavy crudes was seen weighed by upcoming sales of Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) crude and increased supplies from Latin America.
WTI/Midland moved at five cents premium, within the same range as earlier this week, and Light Louisiana Sweet/St James was notionally in the range plus 38/41 cents.
Limited imports into the Gulf Coast continued to lend support to domestic differentials, especially in-season distillate light crudes.
